## Historical audit: S0113

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/sceneevolve_cli/C2/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 is visible; the image files themselves are not visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Line 25, `model_request`, characters [0,144219) | The instructed goal was an editable reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, including camera, architecture, multiple separate objects and materials. The student’s inferred scene was a window-side kitchen; object names and estimated anchors are not independent confirmation of the photograph. |
| Line 25, prior student programs and runner results | The first program built grouped window, cabinet, counter/sink, towel, roll, appliances and jug geometry; it specified stone noise, metallic and translucent finishes, camera and lights. It modeled connections such as towel/ring, pitcher handle and tap as grouped parts, and tilted the blender cup and pitcher lid. These constructions do not establish that the parts actually connect correctly or match the reference pose. Step 1 returned `ok: true` and a saved render. |
| Line 25, student visual audit and revision | The student reported an oversized roll, displaced jug, narrow towel and pale render, diagnosing camera framing as dominant while also noting local geometry and brightness. It proposed a wider lens, altered viewing angle and broader towel. The next program adopted the lens change from 57 to 49 mm and broadened the towel, but retained camera position, explicitly rejecting the orbit as potentially worsening jug parallax; it also raised the cabinet bottom. Step 2 returned `ok: true`. |
| Line 25, next student program and runner result | The student claimed the widening moved roll and jug inward, while discrepancies remained. It moved the jug, shortened the roll, revised the towel and ring, and reduced exposure to -1.15. Step 3 returned `ok: true`; this confirms execution and saved output, not the claimed visual improvement. |
| Line 26, `codex_session`, characters [0,7676); lines 27–28, characters [0,352) and [0,59) | The final read-only student session completed with zero tool calls. The student answered `SELECT 3`; the subsequent select event records step 3. This is a selection, not an independent quality assessment. |

**Teacher input and exploration.** No separately identified teacher message is visible in this chunk. The visible audit was the student’s own response to a user instruction, and its subsequent code shows partial adoption. The student explored through three successive builds and its own image-comparison claims; the final session had no tools. Earlier unseen chunks cannot establish additional teacher receipt or intervention.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Formally, three builds succeeded and step 3 was selected; execution budget exhaustion was a planned constraint, not evidence of an algorithm failure or technical interruption. Visual correctness remains unknown: neither the images nor independent geometric checks are available here. In particular, actual object completeness, part attachment, occlusion, pose, material appearance, camera alignment and whether exposure improved the render remain unresolved.

**Lessons.** Transferable: distinguish execution success from visual fidelity, and test shared framing hypotheses separately from local geometry. Task-specific: the proposed jug, roll, towel and exposure corrections address this student’s reported discrepancies; whether they worked remains a hypothesis, not a verified result.
